title: callback-id-collision-after-routing-fallback-corrupts-structured-tool-output
text:
callback-id-collision-after-routing-fallback-corrupts-structured-tool-output

description:
Production customer (FinReg Solutions) reported intermittent corruption of structured tool call responses after automatic routing fallbacks between model variants and cross-region proxies. The service returns valid JSON objects from the model, but downstream parsers observe swapped array element order and duplicate 'callback_id' values leading to misattributed tool results and downstream failures in the customer's orchestration layer.

impact_summary:
Affected customers running Dedicated with VPC proxying during capacity or region failover see duplicated callback identifiers and out-of-order tool call fragments. Leads to incorrect tool result mapping, automated downstream retries, and in one case a regulatory report ingestion failure. Several high-volume tenants impacted intermittently during peak traffic windows.

steps_to_reproduce:
Customer config: Dedicated tenant, private VPC proxy, tool-calling enabled, model routing policy: latency-fallback -> model-B
Simulate routing fallback: throttle model-A capacity to force smart routing to model-B
Send high-concurrency chat sessions (20+ concurrent sessions) where each message triggers a function/tool call with unique callback_id and expects structured JSON array of responses
Observe the hosted proxy logs and client's parser: verify that some responses contain duplicate callback_id values across different sessions and arrays with elements in unexpected ordering
Reproduce more reliably by inducing rapid proxy failover (kill proxy worker) while a batch of streaming tool-call responses is being emitted

reproduction_logs:
2026-03-01T14:12:07Z PROXY[pid=2178] route: model-A -> model-B (fallback) session=tenant-42 cid=0x9f12
2026-03-01T14:12:07Z RUNTIME[msg] emit: {"callback_id":"cb:84f3", "tool_results": [{"id":"r1", "body": "..."}, {"id":"r2", "body": "..."}] }
2026-03-01T14:12:07Z RUNTIME[msg] emit: {"callback_id":"cb:1a7e", "tool_results": [{"id":"r3", ...}] }
2026-03-01T14:12:07Z PROXY[pid=2178] fragment-rewrite: assigned-session-seq=1024 -> 1031 (re-mapped), note=fast-failover
2026-03-01T14:12:07Z CUSTOMER_PARSER ERROR: duplicate callback id cb:84f3 seen in session stream, dropping mapping for r1 -> causes missing tool response

observed_behavior:
During streaming handoffs the proxy/ingress layer occasionally reassigns or reuses ephemeral callback identifiers when multiplexing fragments across reconnects. The runtime's fragment interleaving logic does not consistently preserve an origin session->callback monotonic mapping under failover, which allows duplicate callback identifiers to appear in overlapping response sequences.

root_cause_hypothesis:
When smart routing triggers a fallback between model variants or a proxy reconnect occurs, the fragment reassembly module reuses an ephemeral internal callback token for performance. Under high concurrency the token namespace collision occurs before the client-visible callback_id is materialized, causing two distinct tool invocations to surface with the same callback_id in downstream streams.

proposed_fix:
1) Stop reusing ephemeral token values across concurrent sessions during fragment reassembly; introduce a collision-resistant callback mapping (namespace by session+seq). 2) Add an idempotency/dedup layer in the streaming envelope parser to detect and log duplicate callback_id emissions and surface metrics. 3) Add a short-term guardrail that forces synchronous boundary flush on fallback events to avoid interleaving. Implement in runtime fragmenter and proxy adapter components.

workaround:
Customers can enable 'sync-fallback' guardrail in Dedicated console (forces a flush and prevents fragment interleaving on fallback) and lower concurrent tool-call burst size until patch is deployed.

rollback_plan:
Revert the fragment reassembly change by feature flag. If instability occurs, flip guardrail to 'safe_sync_on_fallback' = true and route traffic back to model-A (if healthy) or scale capacity to avoid fallback.

qa_checklist:
Unit tests for session+seq namespacing producing unique callback ids
Integration sim: forced fallback with 1000 concurrent tool calls, assert no duplicate callback_id observed
E2E with customer's VPC proxy configuration (staging) replicating their ingress behavior
Load test with controlled proxy failover to ensure ordering preserved and no added latency beyond SLA threshold

rollout_plan:
Canary deploy to low-traffic Dedicated cluster (region: us-west-2) behind a feature flag for 24h, monitor duplicate-callback-rate and parser-error-rate. If stable, expand to other Dedicated clusters over 48h. For Hosted customers, release in staged rollout with migration window communicated in status page.

monitoring_and_alerting:
metric: runtime.fragmenter.duplicate_callback_count >= 1 triggers PagerDuty
log-alert: parser.duplicate_callback detected more than 5 times in 10m
dashboard: callback-id-entropy over time grouped by tenant and region

notes:
Design/PM feedback (Mar 4): prefer conservative guardrail first, then runtime refactor next sprint
Design review (Mar 10): confirmed UI control for guardrail in Dedicated Console; PM requested clear telemetry to show when guardrail is active
On-call found a related but distinct bug (duplicate fragments without callback collision) — added to backlog for later triage
